title: So glad I got to experience more of the @Oregon Shakespeare Festival ...
transcript: I love the Oregon Shakespeare Festival and after thinking I was only going to get to see one show while I was there thanks to the kindness of a few folks I was able to catch three more shows before I left Oregon and thank goodness I did because I enjoyed these shows way more than I enjoyed Merry Wives of Windsor which ultimately was just not for me that review is already up and I was really bummed that I had chosen to see Mary Wives of Windsor over the importance of being earnest and so I was really really grateful that I got to go see importance of being earnest later in the week and this may be one of my favourite productions that I've ever seen of one of my favourite plays now this production of importance of Being Ernest directed by Desdemona Chiang is set in Malaysia during the Victorian era which works so incredibly well and because of the setting you get to see this like very period piece skewering Victorian era British culture through a lens of assimilation and colonialism it was very clear which characters they cast as Asian performers and which characters they cast as white performers down to the details of which characters spoke with which accent but not only was the trauma therapy on point in this production the comedy was so funny I have read this play multiple times I've seen multiple productions and for many scenes it was like I was seeing it for the first time and that is so hard to do in comedy but these performers were incredible like the entire cast and this hands down had my favourite costume design of all the shows I saw by Melissa Torchia Ugh these costumes were stunning and frankly we should bring back ascots I also got to see into the Woods which is uh sort of an evolution of the production that they did in 2014 it's not exactly the same but a lot of elements uh are similar I did not see that version but that's what I've read first of all into the Woods it's one of the greatest musicals ever written and it's just it's always been a part of my life and so it's really fun every time I go see it how I I get something new out of the show and this production made a lot of really bold choices not all of them worked for me but a lot of them did there was this really interesting decision of having the characters start off as essentially just actors and then as the prologue went on they slowly become part of the fairy tale world and then at the end of the show they then return to kind of you know the the actors that they are there was also an audience participation aspect but that was only in the first act and then it kinda went away in the second act and while I thought both choices were interesting to make they didn't really pay off by the end of the show like I feel like if you're gonna make a bold choice there needs to be a strong payoff by the end about why that choice works because if not then it just it sort of feels like a gimmick and that's kind of how I felt about the choices in this production but at the same time there were some choices in this that absolutely did work for me like Cinderella's dress coming on stage was this absolutely magical moment that brought me to tears the choice to bring Rapunzel back on stage for the witches lament in Act 2 just ah heartbreaking so in terms of the direction it was hit or miss for me but when it hit it really really hit and at the end of the day it's it's into the Woods like into the Woods is still a great freaking show even when it's a little bit over directed still still moves me and finally I got to go see Julius Caesar now I have never seen a production of Julius Caesar before I'm really hit or miss on Shakespeare's tragedies sometimes I find them a little bit boring so I was worried about going to see this I should not have been worried Julius Caesar is great Julius Caesar actually maybe my favourite shakespearean tragedy well I'll keep saying maybe because I feel like it was strengthened by the fact that this is my first time with this material now this production of Julius Caesar is an upstart Crow production told with an all female and non binary cast and I do think that there was a difference between some of the cast members that were bringing a masculine energy to their performance and the cast members who were trying to be mad for me the former worked a lot better like I felt like some of the performers were just trying to portray men and that felt so much more inauthentic than the the performers who just brought a very masculine energy to the their performance overall a lot of the performances really worked for me and I was highly entertained the overall design of this production also was just incredible especially the the scenic design was great there was a really great scenic transition from the first act to the second act but my favourite is the sound designed by Caroline Eng from the moment you entered the theatre and throughout the production it sounded like a horror film and the sound design did a really great job of building this tension throughout the scenes especially as the storms were building in the world of this play and similar to into the Woods not all of the directorial choices in terms of blocking worked for me but I thought the choices that were made were still visually stunning even when I didn't think they entirely worked for the production especially with a longer shakespearean tragedy that kind of gets into the weeds of this like political environment I definitely think that that helps to maintain audience interest throughout the show truly Julius Caesar was the biggest surprise of the festival for me I did not expect to enjoy it as much as I did I was worried I was going to be bored and I was anything but as far as tickets go I got a rush ticket for into the Woods for $28 so huge thank you to the couple donations that I got that helped me to be able to afford that ticket and then importance of being Ernest and Julius Caesar were donated to me by somebody working at the festival so huge huge huge thank you to Theo all three of these shows are playing at the Oregon Shakespeare Festival in to October with into the Woods closing on October 11th and importance of being Earnest and Julius Caesar closing a couple weeks after that
